title: Monoceros R2 Molecular Cloud

recognition.text: Published in the NSF NOIRLab image archive. No published rating.

story: A bright red nebula glows just below the center of this image, which shows a portion of the giant Monoceros R2 molecular cloud, in the constellation Monoceros.

Monoceros R2 is a site where massive stars are forming, especially in the area of that bright red nebula. A molecular cloud is a cold, dense reservoir of gas and dust, where gravity can pull material together into clumps that eventually ignite as stars.

Once massive stars form, their intense light energizes the surrounding gas and makes it glow, which is why star-forming regions often stand out in red hydrogen light. Massive stars are relatively rare and short-lived, so places where they are being born are important for understanding how galaxies build up their stars and how those stars shape the clouds around them.

understand.summary: The Blanco 4-meter Telescope's Mosaic II camera used two narrowband filters. Sulfur [S II] is shown in blue and hydrogen-alpha in red.
